title: CGU's ALICE robot flags overpricing in three 2024 Rio de Janeiro federal hospital tenders; one suspended, one revoked, one re-estimated
summary: The CGU's ALICE tool flagged three 2024 federal hospital tenders in Rio de Janeiro state; auditors confirmed R$19.4m of overpricing risk, and one was suspended, one revoked and one re-estimated
account: In March 2023 Fernanda Odilla of the University of Bologna reported in an independent study that Alice has helped auditors stop irregular tenders across Brazil. She did not examine the tenders in this case. ALICE (Analisador de Licitações, Contratos e Editais) is the in-house tool of the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU). It reads procurement documents with artificial-intelligence techniques and issues risk alerts. The national procurement portal shows that tender 90017/2024 was published on 14 August 2024. On 14 January 2025 the CGU reported that ALICE had flagged three 2024 tenders of federal hospitals in Rio de Janeiro state. At the Hospital Federal de Ipanema, tender 90016/2024 for laminated gowns (estimated R$16,726,635.12) was suspended after auditors confirmed an overpricing risk of R$10,925,029.92. Tender 90017/2024 for nursing supplies (estimated R$15,450,714.80) had an overpricing risk of R$5,994,645.60. It was re-estimated at R$12,386,939.96, a saving of R$3,063,774.84. At the Hospital Federal dos Servidores do Estado, tender 90002/2024 (estimated R$26,578,591.02) was revoked after a confirmed risk of R$2,475,054.36. The release gives no total. The three confirmed risks sum to R$19,394,729.88, the R$19.4 million of the headline and summary. The release gives no dates for the suspension and revocation. The portal shows that the hospital bought surgical gloves under tender 90017/2024 in May 2025, after the re-estimate. That record gives no final prices, so it does not show the size of the saving at purchase.
purpose: Continuous automated audit of federal procurement notices to detect risks such as inflated price estimates before contracts are awarded
system: ALICE (Analisador de Licitações, Contratos e Editais), CGU text-mining and AI alert tool
domain: Public administration: government audit and procurement control
segment: Federal internal control (anti-corruption and waste prevention)

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary is named. The beneficiaries are public bodies and, indirectly, taxpayers.

The result mattered to the two hospitals and to the federal budget. One tender saw a documented R$3,063,774.84 reduction. One suspension and one revocation removed R$13.4 million of confirmed overpricing risk.
The effect is small at national scale. The three tenders were among 118,069 processes analyzed in 2024.

ai_role.statement: The CGU release states that each tender “teve alerta do Robô ALICE” and that auditors then confirmed the overpricing risk. The suspension, revocation and re-estimation are described as results of that audit action. Human auditors and hospital managers made the decisions. ALICE's role was detection and triage. Developer and deployer are the same public body, so this is the body documenting its own tool. The CGU page is on record as an archived copy, because the live page was restricted during Brazil's 2026 electoral period.

fields.account: In March 2023 Fernanda Odilla of the University of Bologna reported in an independent study that Alice has helped auditors stop irregular tenders across Brazil. She did not examine the tenders in this case. ALICE (Analisador de Licitações, Contratos e Editais) is the in-house tool of the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU). It reads procurement documents with artificial-intelligence techniques and issues risk alerts. The national procurement portal shows that tender 90017/2024 was published on 14 August 2024. On 14 January 2025 the CGU reported that ALICE had flagged three 2024 tenders of federal hospitals in Rio de Janeiro state. At the Hospital Federal de Ipanema, tender 90016/2024 for laminated gowns (estimated R$16,726,635.12) was suspended after auditors confirmed an overpricing risk of R$10,925,029.92. Tender 90017/2024 for nursing supplies (estimated R$15,450,714.80) had an overpricing risk of R$5,994,645.60. It was re-estimated at R$12,386,939.96, a saving of R$3,063,774.84. At the Hospital Federal dos Servidores do Estado, tender 90002/2024 (estimated R$26,578,591.02) was revoked after a confirmed risk of R$2,475,054.36. The release gives no total. The three confirmed risks sum to R$19,394,729.88, the R$19.4 million of the headline and summary. The release gives no dates for the suspension and revocation. The portal shows that the hospital bought surgical gloves under tender 90017/2024 in May 2025, after the re-estimate. That record gives no final prices, so it does not show the size of the saving at purchase.

The result mattered to the two hospitals and to the federal budget. One tender saw a documented R$3,063,774.84 reduction. One suspension and one revocation removed R$13.4 million of confirmed overpricing risk.
The effect is small at national scale. The three tenders were among 118,069 processes analyzed in 2024.

Audit capacity must exist to act on alerts before award
Reference prices must be available to confirm overpricing

echoes.setting: Hospital Federal de Ipanema glove tender (Pregão 15/2021), CGU audit with ALICE support, reported 4 October 2023

Federal road-works engineering tender: about R$100 million cut from the reference value after an ALICE alert (CGU, 30 December 2024); the release gives no date for this tender, so the year is inferred from the 2024 year-end release

TCE-MG state-level use of Alice: in December 2022 TCE-MG published the result of an audit covering 2,297 state and municipal tenders in August 2022 alone, with corrections to notices worth R$91,723,011.31 (Atricon, 28 June 2023; publication month only)
